# SockTuner 0.9.0-beta.2

## UDP quality and experimental presets

- Measure UDP upload and download loss separately, plus RTT median/P95, jitter, late echoes, duplicates, reordering and locally delayed sends.
- Save a baseline, repeat under matching conditions and export the result without the responder key. Tuning writes are disabled while a UDP measurement runs.
- The portable ZIP now includes a self-contained Windows x64 responder in `UdpResponder/`. Run it on another computer you choose; its README explains the shared key, firewall scope and command-line client. A responder on your LAN tests the local path; an Internet test needs an external endpoint.
- Choose the new balanced gaming preset or an explicit aggressive experimental trial. The aggressive preset includes LSO/coalescing/interrupt options and selected Intel/Realtek templates, subject to the live driver's accepted values and vendor labels.
- Experimental templates stay visibly unverified on uncharacterised hardware and require confirmation. Their source is retained through preview and audit; they do not mark a device as verified.
- New power plans use advertised controls instead of automatically writing `PnPCapabilities=24`, preserving wake-on-LAN. The legacy backend remains available for old audit recovery. EnablePME stays a separate manual wake control.

## Validation

989 .NET tests passed, with 14 pre-existing skips. Windows UI tests exercised two 600-packet local runs, baseline comparison, cancellation and the write guard. Protocol tests cover direction-specific loss, authentication, malformed packets, missing summaries, retries, duplicate/reordered/late echoes and cancellation.

Two real PC-to-Windows-11-VM LAN runs each delivered 600/600 packets, with no observed upload/download loss, late echoes or local scheduling delays. No preset was applied between these runs. This verifies the transport and comparison path; it does not establish physical-NIC tuning benefits or Internet-path quality.

## Requirements, upgrade and limits

Windows 10 22H2 or supported Windows 11, x64. Extract the portable ZIP and start `SockTuner.exe`. Both executables are self-contained; no separate .NET installation is required. Enable Advanced mode to open UDP quality.

Existing settings are preserved. Selecting the balanced preset leaves offloads as they currently are; it does not undo an earlier aggressive preset. Use audit rollback to restore recorded values. The UDP responder is opt-in and does not create firewall/router rules or install a background service.

This is an unsigned community beta. Verify the ZIP against the published SHA-256 checksum. Automatic installation of updates remains unavailable until the publisher-signature requirements are satisfied. Experimental tuning can interrupt the selected link and has no guaranteed performance benefit.
